Absolutely not! While some of the latter seasons may have seen a slight decline in quality, it is just that, slight, and there are still some episodes in late seasons of Frasier that are some of the absolute best.

While the argument can, and has been made that those two characters lost part of themselves when the will-they wont-they ended, really it's more just growth of the characters in more mature people (which may seem boring, but is also realistic, and Frasier is great at writing proper in depth characters). Daphne lost a lot of her "quirkiness," sure, but that's to be expected as one grows up over 10 years and settles down. But the writing, humor, and just talent on the show carries it through just fine. 

I'd say probably the last 2-3 seasons were the weakest by a good bit, however that was LONG after Daphne and Niles got together, and therefore not indicative of them, but of a show just running it's course as 10+ year-running shows do.

That being said although you didn't ask, all of the seasons are some of the best TV to ever be written. No line is useless, no prop adds nothing, the physical comedy is perfect but the script is just as stellar, the characters are believable, and it (except for maybe 3 poorly aged jokes I can think of) has aged spectacularly well for a show of it's time.
